reading.title: The night bus
reading.text: The cheapest way to cross the country is the night bus, and everyone who has taken it once has an opinion about it. You leave at eleven, you arrive at six, and in between you try to sleep sitting up while the air conditioning fights the tropical night. The advantage is obvious: you save the price of a hotel, and you wake up already in the city you wanted to reach. The disadvantage arrives about an hour later, when you realise you cannot check in until two in the afternoon and you are carrying your luggage around a city that is still waking up. Experienced travellers do one of two things. They book a hotel that keeps bags for arriving guests, or they plan the first morning as something that needs no energy at all: a long breakfast, a park, a slow walk. What they never do is plan a museum.
